note: Authored word and phrase sets for languages ASJP does not reach.

egyp1246.note: Hieroglyphs with Egyptological transliteration. Vowels are not written, so the readings are conventional rather than reconstructed pronunciation.
items: the speech of Egypt — the language's own name
the great house — the word English took as pharaoh
good, beautiful, complete — the nefer of Nefertiti
may he live, be prosperous and healthy — written after a king's name

midd1317.note: Spelling was not standardised; these are common forms.
items: Whan that Aprille with his shoures soote
when April with its sweet showers — the opening of the Canterbury Tales

oldf1239.note: Two-case Old French; forms vary by region and date.
items: Carles li reis, nostre emperere magnes
Charles the king, our great emperor — the opening of the Chanson de Roland

latv1249.note: Latvian is living; ASJP simply never sampled it.

clas1254.note: Wylie transliteration beside the Tibetan script. The spelling froze in the seventh century, so written clusters are no longer pronounced.
items: awakened one — the word used for Buddha

impe1235.note: Given in square script, the form most Aramaic was later copied in.
